bearings.paper_claim: Bill numbers and titles extracted from LD-2 Section 16 are matched by distance measures to the Bills component (421,764 bills, 6th-119th Congress); low-confidence matches get extra scrutiny. The linkage is said to detect significantly more bill lobbying than Kim and Kunisky 2021 and to capture ex-post lobbying. The main text gives no match count, precision, recall or threshold.
bearings.paper_location: Intro p.4-5 (text lines 176-188); Bills p.6 (lines 233-234); Technical Validation p.8 (lines 408-416)
bearings.system_side: build_network_2021_rebuild.py credits every sponsor and cosponsor of each lobbied bill (line 13). Generous outputs keep ambiguous-title fan-out; strict outputs need a same-segment formal citation. Slash-joined citations parse only the left side (line 19; 2 of 376 distinct bills, 0.5 percent, 2023-24 association corpus). LD-2 has no member or position field (lobby_interactions.py line 18).
bearings.transfer_conditions: BICAM fits only as a candidate second path for bill-mention resolution. A bill-to-sponsor join from it is a roster edge with P(credited given lobbied) = 1 by construction and adds no contact signal. Precision and recall sit in the Supplementary Information, which this check did not have.
bearings.verifier_note: The paper says matches target the Bills component of 421,764 bills; it does not say that many bills were matched. The code lines and the 0.5 percent figure reproduce exactly. The analyst left out the generous versus strict split in the network output.

bearings.paper_claim: BICAM supplies Bill-LDA linkages, not the LDA filings, and points to LobbyView and OpenSecrets as the compilations of LDA data. Members are keyed by bioguide_id and icpsr. Discrepancies between the two APIs, such as GovInfo missing bioguide_id for nickname members, are fixed by a rules-based merge.
bearings.paper_location: Background p.3-4 (lines 89-94, 177-178); Members p.6 (lines 259-266); Technical Validation p.8 (lines 398-407)
bearings.system_side: collect_lobbyview.py is a standalone ingest of the LobbyView export dated 2024-10-25 (VINTAGE, line 73). The n_bills caveat at line 446 describes sponsored or cosponsored attention to bills, not disclosed contact.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Context only. BICAM does not replace the client or filer source. Any post-2021 bill linkage from it would serve identity resolution, not classification input.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper statements reproduce. The paper does not tie its rules-based merge to the 2,597 member count. The 2024-10-25 vintage is confirmed in code. The reliability-through-2021 claim was not found in the code read or the paper, so it is dropped here.

bearings.paper_claim: Bulk bills, amendments, committees and members from the official APIs with rolling updates. Retrieving the full set directly needs over 100 endpoints, a 5,000 requests per hour cap, and at least 10 requests per bill.
bearings.paper_location: Background p.3 (lines 114-116); Methods p.4 (lines 133-137); Data Records p.6-7
bearings.system_side: sync_sentinel_bill_ledger.py decay_weight gives 1.0 for Congress 119, 0.8 for 118 and 0.64 for 117, described in the code as the frozen legacy archive schedule. The code read does not show that this weight feeds the activity score. The congress.gov search-URL scraping in R was not inspected.

bearings.verifier_note: API figures reproduce. The 0.8 is one step of a 1.0, 0.8, 0.64 schedule rather than a single frozen rate, and the link from that schedule to the activity counts is not shown in the cited code.

summary_issues: The summary implies the Bill-to-LDA linkage reaches 421,764 bills. The paper names the Bills component as the match target and gives no match count.

The summary calls BICAM a second independent path for bill resolution. BICAM uses the same kind of LDA text extraction, so it is a comparator until its precision and recall are read from the Supplementary Information.
The summary says Melange credits every sponsor and cosponsor. The network has generous and strict variants that disambiguate titles differently.
The summary ties a frozen 0.8 decay to the activity counts. The code shows a 1.0, 0.8, 0.64 schedule written as a weight on ledger rows, and the feed into the activity score is not shown.
The summary says finance-client classification is reliable through 2021. This was not found in the code read or the paper.

Not in the summary: ext.json lists the 123,061 amendments under the Bills component, and lists Lauderdale and Clark 2014 as a linkage BICAM makes. BICAM cites that paper only as text-scaling research (refs 24-26).
